newsitem.title: USA: MCA/Viacom cable dispute trial to begin.
newsitem.headline: MCA/Viacom cable dispute trial to begin.

text.p: Trial was to begin today in the dispute between Seagram Co Ltd and Viacom Inc over the 1981 joint cable venture, USA Networks, which the companies inherited in recent acquisitions.

Seagram's MCA Inc unit alleges that Viacom's ownership of basic cable television networks and pay-per-view programming services violates the non-compete obligation of its Paramount Communications Inc unit under the joint venture.
As a remedy, Seagram, which owns no other cable interests, wants Viacom to sell its 50 percent stake is USA Networks to MCA.
In a counterclaim lawsuit, Viacom accuses MCA of unfair competition and seeks damages for MCA's alleged breach of fiduciary duty in the partnership.
In court papers, Viacom says MCA is "attempting to garner whatever leverage it can find to force Viacom to sell (its share of USA Networks) cheap when Viacom had no desire to sell at all."

MCA contends that Viacom's ownership of MTV, VH-1/Video Hits One, Nickelodeon/Nick at Nite, and Comedy Central's pay-per-view programming triggers a buy/sell provision of the joint venture. In court papers, MCA says that under that provision, Viacom can sell its half of USA Networks to MCA or a third party at the lower end of an independent valuation, or buy MCA's half at the higher end of the valuation.

The list of potential trial witnesses includes Seagram Chief Executive Edgar Bronfman Jr, former MCA head Sidney Sheinberg, Viacom Chairman Sumner Redstone, television producer Aaron Spelling, celebrity lawyer Howard Weitzman, and MCA Chief Executive Frank Biondi, a former chief executive of Viacom.

Also before the court is Viacom's motion for a ruling to validate its assertion that it "agreed to release Frank Biondi from the non-competition provisions in his employment contract to enable him to be hired by MCA...in exchange for MCA's waiver" of claims arising from Viacom's ownership of the MTV networks.
The lawsuits were filed in April in Delaware Chancery Court. Vice Chancellor Myron Steele has set November 8 as the final day of the non-jury trial.
